text:
Barrett Hayton's line looks ordinary: four goals and 13 points in 24 games. The ice tells a better story. Utah takes 63% of the 5v5 expected goals with him on, nine points better than when he sits, on a workload of 14:50 a night.

His own finishing is what's missing. He is shooting 8.7%, below the bottom of his talent range, on chances (0.95 expected goals per 60) that say more should have gone in. Three goals in his last ten, including a third-period equalizer against Vancouver and a goal that forced overtime against San Jose, suggest it is starting to turn.

Evolving-Hockey liked his defense last season (opponents got fewer chances with him out, 89th percentile), and Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking has him on the end of a lot of royal-road passes, the cross-slot feeds that go in 25% of the time. The fifth pick of 2018 has settled into a useful two-way center; the goals may catch up with the process.
headline: Barrett Hayton is winning his shifts, not his shots
